<reason>A gives the stronger comparative case: negotiated deadlines, binding support, and early milestones can improve investment incentives without requiring blackouts when implementation fails. A answers both pressure questions directly, including acknowledging that inadequate financing defeats the package. B raises legitimate construction and financing risks, but repeatedly assumes that imperfect compliance makes binding obligations worthless. Its claim that a feasible common endpoint is merely a label also insufficiently answers A’s account of reciprocal support and accountability.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s distinction between breaching an obligation and having no obligation breaks B’s blackout-or-theatre dilemma. B responds by calling the surviving obligation paperwork, rather than explaining why corrective requirements and consequences cannot influence financing and construction before the deadline.</best_rebuttal>
